stories.title: Tamil Nadu BJP chief welcomes Supreme Court order to light Deepam at Deepathoon
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu BJP chief welcomes Supreme Court order to light Deepam at Deepathoon
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: Tamil Nadu BJP chief Nainar Nagendran added that the Supreme Court could be approached again if the lamp was left unlit.
Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagendran on Friday welcomed the Supreme Court’s order to light the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon on Madurai’s Thiruparankundram hill on November 28.
Speaking to India Today, Nagendran said he expected the lamp to be lit on Saturday and indicated that the Supreme Court could be approached again if its order was not carried out.
Asked about his earlier remarks linking the row to Chief Minister Vijay’s Christian faith, Nagendran said Vijay was not personally responsible for lighting the lamp.
The dispute is over where on the hill the lamp should be lit.

The Tamil Nadu government says the traditional site is the mandapam near the Uchippillayar shrine, while petitioners have sought to light it at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar higher up the hill near a dargah.
The bench said the failure to light the lamp at the pillar on November 24 appeared to be wilful disobedience of its November 20 order.

It issued contempt notices to Tamil Nadu’s Chief Secretary, the Director General of Police and 13 others, asking them to appear on December 15 and explain why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against them.
The court suspended the board of trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and appointed retired High Court judges Vaidyanathan and Parthiban to take over its administration.
It handed security of the hill to the Central Reserve.
Police Force and directed it to ensure that devotees could visit the dargah and perform their rituals.
The court directed the retired judges to consult temple functionaries and, if the flame at the Uchippillayar mandapam was still burning, use it to light the Deepam at the pillar.

stories.headline: RBI Guv to MSMEs: Take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs
stories.title: RBI Guv to MSMEs: Take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs
stories.summary: Malhotra observed that only about 20–30 per cent of eligible Indian exports take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Friday exhorted MSMEs (micro, small and medium enterprises) to look beyond domestic markets and take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs (Free Trade Agreements).
In his address at the SME Finance & Investment Summit, Malhotra observed that only about 20–30 per cent of eligible Indian exports take advantage of the lower tariffs available under India’s FTAs.
This is remarkably low compared with 60–70 per cent utilisation by partner countries’ exports to India.
“It is an opportunity we are leaving on the table.
Learn about the FTAs relevant to your products, invest in quality, standards and certification, and draw on the support available from the agencies concerned,” he said.
The Governor highlighted the importance of formalising the financials of MSMEs and earning the confidence of their lenders.
“Every lasting business relationship rests on trust.
Customers stay with you because you deliver quality on time; suppliers stay with you because you keep your commitments.
Lenders are no different.
“You will obtain credit on better terms if you keep proper accounts, file returns on time, transact digitally and manage your finances with discipline.
Increasingly, the data trail your business leaves behind will count for as much as the assets you can pledge,” he said.
Malhotra encouraged the MSMEs to use the instruments built for them and treat support as a catalyst, not a crutch.

stories.headline: Supreme Court orders Karthigai Deepam to be lit on ‘deepathoon’ on November 28; issues contempt notice
stories.title: Supreme Court orders Karthigai Deepam to be lit on ‘deepathoon’ on November 28; issues contempt notice
stories.summary: Bench directs Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, Madurai District Collector, temple authorities to be present for next hearing on Dec. 15; court sees ‘pre-meditated conspiracy' between State and temple trustees
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Rejecting the Tamil Nadu government’s claim that it stayed aloof from the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple management’s customary decisions, the Supreme Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) said non-compliance with its November 20 order to light the Karthigai Deepam on the ‘deepathoon’ (stone pillar) atop the Thirupparankundram Hill in Madurai amounted to “wilful disobedience” born of a “pre-meditated conspiracy” between the State and the temple trustees.

A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi ordered the Board of Trustees of the temple to be suspended before appointing two former High Court judges – former Chief Justice of Meghalaya High Court S. Vaidyanathan and former Madras High Court judge Justice V. Parthiban - to act as Receivers.
The court directed the Karthigai Deepam to be lit again on Saturday (November 28, 2026), this time on the stone pillar, as was originally ordered on November 20.
Central forces would provide security.
The Receivers have to ensure the ceremony is carried out in consultation with the temple stanikars.
However, the interim order would not grant any future equities in favour of any party.
The court made clear that its order was limited only to contempt petitions.
The main case on religious rights concerning the Thirupparankundram lamp-lighting row would be heard in the second week of January 2027.
The row stems from the claims of ownership over the hilltop.
The ‘deepathoon’ is located near the Sikandar Badusha Dargah on top of the hill, while the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple is at the base of the hill.
The dargah side has claimed ownership of the hilltop, including the deepathoon site.
The court order comes two days after the ceremonial lamp was lit at the customary location – Deepa Mandapam – atop the hill and not as the Bench mandated.

stories.headline: Supreme Court grants bail to former AAP legislator Naresh Balyan
stories.title: Supreme Court grants bail to former AAP legislator Naresh Balyan
stories.summary: A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh passed the order while hearing Mr. Balyan’s plea challenging a Delhi High Court order denying him bail in the case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) granted bail to former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) legislator Naresh Balyan, who was booked under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) over his alleged association with U.K.-based gangster Kapil Sangwan.
A Bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh, while granting bail, directed Mr. Balyan to cooperate with the trial proceedings.
Mr. Balyan had approached the court after the Delhi High Court rejected his bail plea.
In August, the High Court had denied Mr. Balyan bail, observing that the registration of 17 FIRs against the alleged crime syndicate was indicative of “continuing unlawful activity” under the MCOCA.
Justice Manoj Jain had further held that prolonged incarceration could not be the sole consideration for granting bail in cases involving serious offences under stringent penal statutes.
During the hearing, senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for Mr. Balyan along with advocate Vivek Jain, submitted that key prosecution witnesses had retracted their statements.

He also pointed out that Mr. Balyan had himself lodged a complaint with the police alleging threats from the very gangster with whom he was accused of having links, following which he was provided police protection.
Opposing the bail plea, Additional Solicitor General Raja Thakare, appearing for the Delhi.
Police, submitted that the case involved serious allegations of organised crime, including land grabbing and extortion.

He argued that the applicability of the MCOCA did not hinge on the registration of multiple cases against an individual accused but on the criminal activities of the organised crime syndicate, against which, he said, 19 cases had been registered.
In his petition, Mr. Balyan pointed out that he had been in custody since December 2025 and that the investigation against him was complete.
He further contended that the evidence relied upon by the prosecution was inadmissible and that he had not initially been named in the case.

stories.headline: Naidu in Delhi for NDA meeting after Union Cabinet clears delimitation Bill with 50% rise in seats for all States
stories.title: Naidu in Delhi for NDA meeting after Union Cabinet clears delimitation Bill with 50% rise in seats for all States
stories.summary: Chandrababu Naidu joins NDA leaders in Delhi ahead of Parliament’s special sitting, as the Union Cabinet’s Bill keeps the present ratio of seats among States until 2051
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu left for New Delhi on Friday (November 27, 2026) to attend a meeting of National Democratic Alliance (NDA) leaders convened by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, ahead of a special sitting of Parliament.
Mr. Naidu flew to the national capital after chairing a State Cabinet meeting in Amaravati virtually.
“After completing the Cabinet meeting, Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu left for New Delhi, where he will meet with NDA leaders in the evening,” an official release said.
He is also expected to address a press conference in Delhi, sources said.
The Lok Sabha has been reconvened on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2 for a special sitting to transact essential business, which the government proposed on Thursday.

On Friday, the Union Cabinet approved a Constitution Amendment Bill providing for women’s reservation through delimitation, with an equal, proportionate increase of 50% in seats across all States and the present ratio of seats among States to be kept until 2051.

The Bill and the Women’s Reservation Act are expected to figure prominently at the NDA meeting, along with concerns over the possible impact of delimitation on the parliamentary representation of southern States.
The allies are also expected to coordinate their positions on matters affecting the States.
Mr. Naidu has been attending periodic meetings of NDA constituents since the TDP rejoined the alliance ahead of the 2024 elections.

He took part in the meeting convened by Mr. Modi in June 2024 to discuss government formation, and in meetings of alliance leaders in December 2024 and February 2025 on coordination among partners and political issues.
He also attended an NDA partners’ meeting at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi in June 2026.

stories.headline: MP Choudhary Ramzan records 91% attendance in Rajya Sabha
stories.title: MP Choudhary Ramzan records 91% attendance in Rajya Sabha
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 27: National Conference (NC) Rajya Sabha MP Chowdry Mohammad Ramzan recorded 91 per cent attendance, participated in 21 debates and raised 32 questions during his first three parliamentary sessions, with issues concerning Jammu and Kashmir’s infrastructure, employment, agriculture and environmental security featuring prominently in his parliamentary interventions. According to parliamentary performance data compiled by PRS Legislative Research, Ramzan’s attendance stood 11 percentage points above the national average of 80 per cent and four percentage points above Jammu and Kashmir’s average of 87 per cent. Ramzan, who took oath on December 1, 2025, participated in the Winter Session of 2025, followed by the Budget and Monsoon sessions of 2026, covering 45 parliamentary sittings up to August 13, 2026. His parliamentary participation came despite disruptions during the Monsoon Session, which affected the conduct of parliamentary business. Among the key issues raised by the MP were the construction of the Sadhna and Razdan Pass tunnels, all-weather connectivity to isolated border regions, the proposed Sopore-Kupwara railway link, extension of the Baramulla railway line and the Bandipora-Lolab road project. Ramzan also sought details from the Centre on stalled bridge and tunnel projects in rural Jammu and Kashmir, road connectivity between Machil and Tangdhar via Keran, and the inclusion of Bungus Valley under the National Ropeways Development Programme. Employment and economic concerns featured prominently in his parliamentary questions, with the MP seeking details regarding a special employment package for Jammu and Kashmir, safeguards for horticultural crops in view of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and the promotion of high-density plantations. During parliamentary proceedings, Ramzan raised concerns over the threat to Kashmir’s horticulture industry from harmful agrochemicals and apple imports, besides flagging issues concerning hydroelectric power projects, particularly in the Chenab Valley. On environmental and public welfare issues, the MP sought information regarding Jammu and Kashmir’s vulnerability to Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), the drinking water crisis, drug addiction surveys and seizures, and micro-irrigation facilities. His parliamentary interventions also covered school education infrastructure, telecom services, tourism promotion in Kupwara, the status and completion timeline of Government Medical College Handwara and the operationalisation of the Khelo India Excellence Centre at Gulmarg. Beyond region-specific matters, Ramzan participated in discussions on the Union Budget 2026–27, the Motion of Thanks on the President’s Address, the functioning of the Ministry of Rural Development and several legislative proposals. These included Bills concerning public examinations, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, Central Armed Police Forces, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and the strength of Supreme Court judges. Through Special Mentions and other parliamentary interventions, Ramzan also raised the demand for granting classical language status to Kashmiri, the attack on former Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah, the need to uphold communal harmony and the safety and evacuation of Indian nationals from Gulf countries.

stories.summary: Rohit Sharma will return as Mumbai Indians captain for IPL 2027 following Hardik Pandya's trade to Punjab Kings. The five-time IPL-winning skipper, who was replaced by Hardik ahead of the 2024 season, returns to the leadership role after three seasons. Rohit, who joined Mumbai Indians in 2011 and took over the captaincy in 2013, will lead the franchise in its 20th season of the IPL, chasing a sixth IPL title.
